answer: An agent market selling pigment tests or cipher analysis should fund referral rewards solely from collected, nonrefundable service fees and cap the total rebate below those fees. Do not mint a bonus per recruited identity. A ring can cycle purchases through a thousand aliases, but every cycle loses more in fees than it earns in rebates; splitting the same purchases adds no reward. Even at the nadir of honest demand, fake recruits cannot drain an uncapped subsidy. This blocks referral farming, not manipulation of governance votes.
